message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me not to want to attend my great aunt's funeral. Let me start by understanding the situation better. I just came home from college in Britain, which is like being in high school in America. When I walked in, my mum told me that her grandma's sister, who is my great aunt Wyn, has died. The funeral will probably be soon. My first thoughts were, "Who?" and "Why is she telling me this?" I've never heard this name before, and I don't remember meeting this person except for one time when I was extremely young, like maybe 1 or 2 years old. So, I don't really know who she is or how she's connected to our family. This led to a bit of an argument because my mum wanted me to go to the funeral. I'm really awkward at funerals, especially for people I've only met once or not at all. I don't feel comfortable being there, and I don't see the point of attending if I don't know the person or have any connection to them. My mum's main argument was that I should go out of respect and to support her. But she's never mentioned this great aunt to me before, even though she supposedly played a big role in raising her as my grandmother. It seems like this is one of the few times we'll see the larger branch of the family, and there might be hundreds of people there, but I only know a few of them, maybe 10 at most. To me, it feels like gate-crashing someone else's family funeral. Even though I'm part of the family, I don't think anyone would want me there since I don't know or didn't know the person who died. I don't see how this takes precedence over everything else, and I feel like I have to keep reiterating that I've never met this person beyond that one time when I was a baby. So, the question is: Is it right or wrong for me not to want to attend the funeral of someone who is practically a stranger to me, just because she's family? I think I need to consider a few things here. First, what does "respect" mean in this context? Is it about showing respect for the person who died, or is it about respecting my mum's wishes? Also, what does attending a funeral signify? Is it about being there for the family, or is it about personal closure? I also need to think about my feelings. I'm really uncomfortable with the idea of attending a funeral for someone I don't know. It doesn't feel meaningful to me, and I don't see how it would help anyone. On the other hand, my mum seems to think it's important, and she's trying to guilt-trip me into going. Maybe I should also consider the cultural or familial expectations around funerals. In some cultures, attending funerals is a significant way to show respect and support for the family. But in my personal experience, I don't feel that way about it, especially for someone I don't know. I wonder if there's a middle ground. Could I find a way to show respect without attending the funeral? Maybe sending a card or a message, or talking to my mum about how I can support her in a way that feels comfortable for me. I also need to think about the potential consequences of not attending. How would my mum and the rest of the family feel if I didn't go? Would it cause more conflict or hurt feelings? Or would they understand my perspective if I explained it to them? On the other hand, forcing myself to attend just to please others might not be healthy for me. It's important to respect my own feelings and boundaries, even if it means making tough decisions. I guess I also need to reflect on what I value in relationships. Do I think it's important to attend funerals of distant relatives to maintain family ties, or is it more about having meaningful connections with the people I spend time with? In the end, I need to decide what feels right for me, considering both my feelings and the expectations of others. It's a tough situation, and I don't want to make a decision that I'll regret later.
